## What changes when the angle changes? {#iv5-angle-exploration .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson }


Keep the lengths fixed. Predict whether the scalar product is **positive, zero or negative**.

<div data-geometric="explore"></div>


::: notes
Additional 2-minute predict–explain activity. Fixed lengths |a|=2 and |b|=5, giving a·b=10 cos θ. Start at 60° with the numerical answer hidden. Change θ from 0° to 180°; collect a prediction before manually revealing. Angle changes hide the previous answer. Presets 0°, 90° and 180° support later special cases. Ask: “How can two non-zero vectors have a scalar product of zero?” The cosine factor determines the sign; the lengths are positive. At 90° the value is exactly zero, not a floating-point approximation. Moving or resetting the controls does not reveal the value.
:::
